title: Rearrange Spaces Between Words
statement: `text` is made of words (runs of one or more lowercase letters) and spaces; neighbouring words always have at least one space between them, and there is at least one word. Keep the words in their order and move the spaces around so that every two neighbouring words are separated by the same number of spaces, with that number as large as possible. Spaces that cannot be shared out evenly go after the last word, so the returned string has exactly the same length as `text`. With a single word, all the spaces end up after it.
constraints: text contains only lowercase English letters and ' '
text contains at least one word

tests.name: Test 10
input: a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z

notes:
## Intuition

Only two numbers matter: how many spaces there are and how many words there are. With `k` words there are `k - 1` gaps, so each gap gets `spaces / (k - 1)` rounded down, and the remainder goes at the end. A single word has no gaps, so every space trails it. A brute force could hand out spaces one at a time to the gaps in rounds, but integer division gives the same split at once.

## Approach

1. Count every space in `text` into `spaces`.
2. Split `text` on spaces and drop the empty pieces, leaving the list `words`.
3. If there is only one word, return it followed by all `spaces`.
4. Otherwise `gap` is `spaces` divided by the number of gaps, rounded down, and `extra` is the remainder.
5. Join the words with `gap` spaces and append `extra` spaces.

## Example 1, step by step

`text = "  this   is  a sentence "` holds 2 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 9 spaces, so `spaces = 9`, and `words = ["this", "is", "a", "sentence"]`. There are 3 gaps, so `gap = 9 / 3 = 3` and `extra = 0`. Joining with three spaces gives `"this   is   a   sentence"`, which has the same 24 characters as the input.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to count spaces, one to split and one to join.
- Space: O(n) for the words and the result.

## Pitfalls

- With one word, `words.length - 1` is `0`; dividing by it gives `Infinity` or `NaN`, so handle that case first.
- Splitting on `' '` makes empty strings for leading, trailing and repeated spaces; filter them out.
- The leftover spaces go at the end, never at the start or spread across the first gaps.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `spaces` | total number of spaces in `text` |
| `words` | the words of `text` in order |
| `gap` | spaces placed between each pair of neighbouring words |
| `extra` | spaces left over, placed after the last word |

narration.2: Start a running count of spaces.
narration.3: Look at each character of the text.
narration.8: Split on single spaces and drop the empty pieces that runs of spaces leave behind.
narration.10: A single word has no gaps to fill.
narration.11: So every space goes after it.
narration.13: Share the spaces evenly over the words.length - 1 gaps, rounding down.
narration.14: Whatever cannot be shared evenly is left over.
narration.15: Glue the words with gap spaces and put the leftover spaces at the end.
